articleTitle: Potential of selected Industry 4.0 tools in the field of airport security screening
abstract: In the article, the authors address the possibility of using augmented reality and its potential together with artificial intelligence in air transport, especially in the context of airport security screening. In the introduction, the authors describe what augmented reality is and how it is used. The second chapter describes in detail how this tool works and the individual types available on the market with their brief features. The third chapter deals directly with the concrete use of these technologies at international airports around the world. In the end, the authors summarise the results and describe the advantages and disadvantages of the technologies discussed in the article.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Experimental Operation of the Mobile Aviation Weather Station at Svidnik Airport
abstract: The article presents the results of the assessment (identification, analysis, evaluation) of the experimental operation of the MeteoHelix IoT Pro mobile meteorological station, the Basic version, which the Faculty of Aeronautics at the Technical University of Kosice installed as part of the implementation of new didactic means of aviation meteorology as part of digital education at the faculty and for use for the benefit of the General Aviation. The article contains information on the method of installing the system, its user environment, the examination and visualization of the measured parameters of weather development, and operational modifications according to the requirements of the flying and control personnel. The article presents another concept in expanding the possibilities of the meteorological station in terms of sensory and software, inexpensive equipment of the station for the needs of general aviation, and the aviation component of the Integrated Rescue System of the Slovak Republic.

articleTitle: Optimization of sightseeing flights in the area of High Tatras
abstract: With new trends in aviation everybody tries to be more and more efficient with the highest possibility of being sustainable. This also applies for small general aviation operations such as sightseeing flights. There is a high demand for such flights in the region of High Tatras. Readers are able to find possible options of aircraft suitable for flights in this region and also rules that apply for this area. Authors created possible routes for flights in the area and calculated loss of fuel if flying is done in inefficient way. In the article there is also calculation of excess fuel consumption when not using suitable aircraft. For the article two experimental flights were done to find the optimal route and altitude for the flight. Based on the optimal route and altitude authors found optimal set-up of aircraft and calculated fuel losses.

articleTitle: Verification of the New Standard Instrument Departure routes for Malacky Airport Using Flight Simulator
abstract: The article points to new approaches in the verification of new flight procedures using computer simulations. In the first part, the article deals with the need for the design and construction of new standard instrument departure routes for Malacky - Kuchyňa airport. The second part of the article contains a description of the newly designed tracks. The Materials and Methods section describes the software that helped us create new flight procedures and their subsequent verification. The final part points to the practical outputs from flight simulator, the application of progressive technologies in the creation of new flight procedures with an emphasis on minimizing costs during verification and minimizing the carbon footprint during testing, as software tools were used to verify the designed routes.

articleTitle: The Vessel Tracking Experiment of MRC-100 PocketQube Satellite
abstract: This paper presents a feasibility study carried out on the MRC-100 PocketQube satellite, which aims to track ships by receiving transponder data of vessels using a miniaturized receiver. Although the space segment of the Automatic Identification System exists, they are usually part of a small satellite. So far the smallest receiver was placed on a CubeSat, but at the moment there is no active mission with a receiver in this category. The target of this experiment is to show that a redundant satellite receiver for this safety system can be further reduced in size, power consumption and realized as a PocketQube payload.

articleTitle: Residual Fatigue Life Analysis of Aircraft Structural Elements
abstract: This work focuses on the analysis of crack propagation in the elements of aircraft structures as well as the estimation of the residual life under the effect of cyclic loads of constant amplitude and load spectrum. In addition to conventional finite elements, XFEM (Extended Finite Element Method) is also used to define the crack propagation trajectory itself. Special attention is given to the determination of fracture mechanics parameters of structural components such as stress intensity factors of aircraft cracked lugs. The effect of shape of lug’s surface crack on residual fatigue life is investigated, too. Predictions and computational investigations are performed to determine fatigue life of an attachment lug under load spectrum. The complete computation procedure for the crack propagation analysis using low-cycle fatigue material properties is illustrated with the damaged structural elements. In this research, the strain energy density (SED) method was used to analyze crack propagation. This method uses the Low Cycle Fatigue (LCF) properties of the material, which are also used to estimate the life to initial failure. This ensures significant savings for experimental verification and shortens the time period for the tests themselves.

articleTitle: Aerodrome Controller’s decision support for the approval of UAS operations
abstract: Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) may means potential benefit for airport operations but at the same time, they pose risks when interacting with manned aviation. Airports as potential sites for drone operations have been examined from several perspectives. Many of them in Europe and the United States are in use as test sites, and 10 years ago, a civil-military joint-use airport in Afghanistan allowed drone operations alongside with the civilian and military traffic. In both cases, the safe operation of unmanned and manned flights were solved by procedural separation - in the first case by designating a Special Use Airspace over the airfield dedicated for UAS flights, in the second case a safe distance was defined from a navigational reference point together with runway closure that served as a guarantee of separation. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) considers UASs and their remote pilots as airspace users who should implement and apply the same rules and procedures that manned aviation does. At the same time, their management means high risk due to the lack of separation standards and procedures for air traffic control services. Our research focuses on the controlled aerodrome environment, within which we aim to develop a system to support the Aerodrome Controller (Aerodrome Controller; also referred to as Air Traffic Control Officer ATCO) decisions to issue clearances at an integrated model airport.

articleTitle: Seeing and avoiding drones
abstract: The paper attempts to point out the difficulties with “see and avoid” principle’s adaptability in terms of drone aviation. Visual detectability of drones is hindered by the design (size, shape, colour) of the UAV itself. Flight safety concerns extend to two basic scenarios as crash to the ground and collision to a piloted aircraft. Probability and severity ranges of such harmful events seem to be significant. The author suggests, that risk arising while drones sharing the airspace with conventional aircraft can be mitigated by increased sensibility.

articleTitle: Problems of land occupation near airports in relation to environmental protection
abstract: Ecology in every mode of transport is one of the main challenges for both designers and users of means of transport. Air transport also has a negative impact on the natural environment to a significant extent. This is due to greenhouse gas emissions, noise, energy consumption as well as land occupancy. Unlike other modes of transport, airports are concentrated in one place and not in a vast area, such as a network of roads (motorways) or railways. Airports are located in points, but they have a significant impact on the local environment, e.g., through changes in the landscape. Their area is significant, often exceeding 5 $\mathrm{k}\mathrm{m}^{2}$, and for the correct performance of air operations, this area must be flattened, devoid of trees and shrubs, and additionally it is fenced and inaccessible to both people and animals. The problem of land occupancy, due to the increasingly accurate analysis of the impact of air transport on the environment, is gaining in importance. The article presents the issue of land occupation in the vicinity of the airport, with particular emphasis on private land on the example of the Katowice-Pyrzowice airport.

articleTitle: Securing the Digital Sky: a scenario-driven study on the enhancement of cybersecurity in location-independent aerodrome control systems
abstract: The rapid advancement of technology in aviation business management, notably through the implementation of location-independent aerodrome control systems, is reshaping service efficiency and cost-effectiveness. However, this emphasis on operational enhancements has resulted in a notable gap in cybersecurity incident management proficiency. This study addresses the escalating sophistication of the cybersecurity threat landscape, where malicious actors target critical safety information, posing risks from disruptions to potential catastrophic incidents. The paper employs a specialized conceptualization technique, derived from prior research, to analyze the interplays between malicious software and degraded modes operations in location-independent aerodrome control systems. Rather than predicting attack trajectories, this approach prioritizes the development of training paradigms to rigorously evaluate expertise across engineering, operational, and administrative levels in air traffic management domain. This strategy offers a proactive framework to safeguard critical infrastructures, ensuring uninterrupted, reliable services, and fortifying resilience against potential threats. This methodology promises to cultivate a more secure and adept environment for aerodrome control operations, mitigating vulnerabilities associated with malicious interventions.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Possibility of Using Lignocellulosic Feedstock for the Production of Sustainable Aviation Fuels
abstract: The work is devoted to the estimation of the possibilities of using lignocellulosic biomass for the production of components of sustainable aviation fuels. The current situation in the production of sustainable aviation fuels is presented along with challenges related to its use. Lignocellulosic biomass is considered a promising feedstock for the production of aviation fuels; its composition, as well as possible conversion routes, are analyzed. Emphasis is placed on the levulinic acid as a component received as a result of biomass processing. It is proposed to convert levulinic acid into alkyl levulinates using different simple alcohols to use them as components of sustainable aviation fuels. The method of alkyl levulinates synthesis is described. The basic physical-chemical properties of received products are determined and analyzed. Alkyl levulinates’ properties are compared to conventional jet fuel’s properties. Based on the experimental data, the possibilities of f using lignocellulosic biomass use for sustainable aviation fuel production are substantiated.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Using Predictive Analytics in the Aviation Industry - Case Study
abstract: Predictive analytics allows businesses to predict the future with a certain degree of accuracy. Forecasting the future development of the business and the direction of the business was and is still essential. In today’s turbulent world, prediction has become critical for effective business and futureproofing, and it is reaching its peak in the priorities of individual companies today. The reason for the need for predictive analytics is that companies have to face serious business and supply chain disruptions, sudden changes in demand, and new risks or challenges. Acceptable and accurate forecasts are essential for making adequate decisions in a world where rapid changes and market fluctuations are constant. In the presented article an ARIMA model (created in Python) to forecast gross capital expenditures is used. Based on the results, it was shown that the ARIMA(1,1,1) model is the most suitable model for forecasting air passenger traffic.

articleTitle: Purchase analysis of the air tickets from Košice and Poprad to London Luton
abstract: The aim of this article is to analyse the purchase of airline tickets from a time point of view. Data from the reservation system of a low-cost air carrier were used for the analysis. The obtained data were on three flights from Poprad and Košice to London Luton. Based on this analysis, we were able to determine in which period the most tickets were sold, or which day of the week or time of day passengers preferred to buy a ticket on these flights. To verify the established hypotheses, 1 331 ticket purchases on the flights from Poprad and Košice to London Luton were analysed. The results of the analysis can provide useful information in determining the prices of air transport and thus maximize the income of the air carrier.

articleTitle: Cracking of steel products during dip galvanizing
abstract: The tests were performed on industrial products made of 23MnNiCrMo5-2 steel, characterized by high internal stress generated in their production process during plastic working, heat treatment and calibration. Steel products were subjected to the process of metallization in a zinc bath and in a zinc bath with an addition of 2 wt. % of tin. They were then subjected to a breaking force load. The selected microareas of the resulting fractures were analysed qualitatively and quantitatively. It has been found that in the cases of galvanization of chains in a bath containing an addition of tin no narrowing on the link section was observed, as was the case with fractures of specimens subjected to metallization in a zinc bath. It has been concluded that links broke as a result of cracking and its propagation and penetration of liquid metal into the substrate material during the metallization process. It has also been found that tin concentration at the top of the crack is approximately eight times greater than in the area close to the surface of the coating.

articleTitle: Effect of reduced minimum spacing application on capacity at Václav Havel Airport, Prague
abstract: With the ever-increasing demand for air travel, airspace capacity in the vicinity and relative proximity of airports is reaching its limit. With the progressive development of new technologies and their advancement, industry has reached a situation where it is physically possible to have a large number of aircraft in the airspace. Unfortunately, under current operational conditions, reaching these theoretical capacity values is impossible as it is outside human capability to handle such extreme numbers of aircraft safely and efficiently. This limitation is mainly obvious at peak times when runway and sector capacity is at its limit. This article focuses on the capacity of Václav Havel Airport in Prague (LKPR) and the airspace in its vicinity. It presents a proposal to apply a reduced horizontal separation minimum on the final approach phase of instrument flight rules (IFR) flights down to 2.5 NM. Also, it evaluates the impact of this reduction and describes the necessary changes in airport infrastructure, legislation, and air traffic control unit procedures. The implementation proposal is based on the practices at airports abroad with a reduced 2.5NM spacing already applied. The experiments carried out showed that the idea of reduced spacing at LKPR is feasible and brings an increase airspace capacity while maintaining an adequate level of safety. Under ideal conditions and traffic composition, an increase in the number of aircraft handled by more than 10% per hour can be reached.

articleTitle: The Possibilities of Using Generative Optimalization in the Design of CubeSats
abstract: The fusion of aerospace component design with the computational capabilities of contemporary computers, capable of handling numerous simulations, opens up entirely new horizons for designers. These possibilities often surpass the constraints of traditional manufacturing methods. Generative design, in particular, paves the way for revolutionary design concepts, drawing inspiration from nature to create unique and innovative solutions. In light of this, it becomes evident that this modern design approach has the potential to bring about a significant paradigm shift in the design process. Such a transformation would be unattainable without the advancement of modern manufacturing technologies, like additive manufacturing, which are gradually becoming integral to the design of components across various industries, not just aviation. This article explores the utilization of generative design optimalization with additive manufacturing methods in the design and production of Supporting components of the passive stabilization system of a CubeSat-class nanosatellite, with a focus on optimizing material consumption and production time.

articleTitle: Concept of Improved UAV Pilots Training
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are becoming increasingly popular in a wide range of applications. To ensure the smooth and, above all, safe operation of air traffic despite the increasing number of UAV users, there is an effort to create suitable conditions for their theoretical and practical training. To this end, several software solutions have been created and tested that are being integrated into the education process. This paper presents three systems, which test the UAV remote pilots in different scenarios, starting with basic stick movements, through simulated flights to flights with a real UAV indoors, along predetermined trajectories. The results of these measurements are analyzed end evaluated using the parameters of the human model.

articleTitle: Analysis of the aviation complex using the identification observer
abstract: The contribution is devoted to the design of the identification observer from its mathematical description through the methodology of synthesis to simulation experiments. Experiments are focused on specific cases of observation-measurement of state variables of linear time-invariant deterministic objects. Simulation experiments are verified on a dynamic object that has the character of an aviation complex.

articleTitle: Selected aspects of UAV group flight trajectory modeling
abstract: In this work, we present the methodology for creating a model of the movement of five flying UAVs that fly in a set formation. The movement of the UAV is modeled in the geocentric coordinate system (ECEF - Earth-Centered, Earth-Fixed). Such models are suitable for planning the movement of several UAVs when monitoring the terrain of interest or searching for objects. The methodology of creating models includes the creation of algorithms for the movement of five UAVs in the selected coordinate system and the selected assembly. The flight trajectories of five UAVs were formed by a straight flight section and several curvilinear flight sections. UAVs were assumed to fly in formations with a designated group leader. Also, the flight parameters of the UAV wm be similar to those of the General Atomics MQ - 9 Reaper type UAV, while the flight height wm be constant. In the presented work, we present one of the possible approaches to the creation of UAV movement models in a specified assembly. Flight simulations of five UAVs were performed using Matlab software.

articleTitle: Digitalization in Aviation MRO Training
abstract: In the realm of aviation Maintenance, Repair, and Operations (MRO) training, the integration of digital technologies offers a transformative response to industry dynamics. This research delves into this paradigm shift, anchored in the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) methodology. Through meticulous examination of diverse aviation experts representing various job roles and expertise contexts, this study unveils insightful revelations. User satisfaction emerges as a focal point, aligning with the need for enhanced contentment. The analysis accentuates the technical feasibility of digital integration, emphasizing compatibility, reliability, and seamless assimilation within established systems. Expert-derived weights and rankings enhance findings, serving as a foundation for informed decision-making in MRO training digitalization. This synthesis emphasizes aviation’s imperative to leverage digitalization, fostering adept professionals capable of navigating contemporary aircraft systems while accommodating diverse job roles and experience levels.

articleTitle: The redundant attitude control system of MRC-100 PocketQube satellite
abstract: In this article the magnetic attitude control system of MRC-100 – a 3 unit PocketQube satellite – is presented. Custom machined ferromagnetic core and air core magnetorquers are used to produce angular momentum in the satellite body utilizing Earth’s magnetic field on Low Earth Orbit. The PocketQube standard limits the size of the available space so all magnetorquers are carefully designed to meet the requirements while staying within the power budget. A prototype is realized to validate the concept of the tiny magnetorquer before integrating it into the flight model. It is repurposed as educational material for space engineering master course students.

articleTitle: Extended Reality possibilities in Air Traffic Management
abstract: In response to the current challenges of aviation we decided to develop an Air traffic controller decision support system with extended reality presentation at the prototype level for demonstration purposes. We would like to show in our paper the initialization phase of this research. We tested several types of extended reality hardware and software, and found that they could not completely support our research, so we decided to develop a custom software to meet our needs. We created the conceptional diagram of the planned system, and the base for airspace visualization.

articleTitle: Analyzing Effects of Chaotic Impulse and Narrowband interference on Galileo E5 signal
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of narrowband interference and chaotic impulsive interference on the Galileo E5 signal. Models for the E5 signal and interference using an additive mixture were created and combined for research. Using the available data, spectral structures for interference were created, which were subsequently integrated into the E5 signal using the Matlab program. The main purpose of the study was to investigate how narrowband interference and chaotic impulse interference affect the power spectral density of the E5 signal. The findings from this research have the potential to be used in the development of robust receivers and signal architectures that can effectively deal with this type of interference.

articleTitle: Selection of Infection Assessment Site Using Fishbone Diagram
abstract: Infection assessment is an important part of healthcare that helps in the diagnosis and treatment of various medical conditions. Choosing the most appropriate site for infection assessment is essential for accurate and timely diagnosis, reducing the risk of complications and improving patient treatment outcomes. In aviation, it is very important to avoid economic losses, and these also arise when staff are absent. In this paper presents a novel approach to guide the selection of sites for infection assessment using a fishbone diagram in an aircraft repair and maintenance facility. This research explores the creation and use of a fishbone diagram specific to infection assessment with factors divided into branches such as patient characteristics, infection type, workspace, and clinical context. By visually representing these factors, the fishbone diagram aids in organizing complex information and offers a structured approach to decision-making and actual planning of maintenance interventions. The paper highlights the potential of using the fishbone diagram as a decision support tool for infection site selection in aircraft repair and maintenance facilities and introduces the detailed methodology and results presented in the full research paper.

articleTitle: Concept of a rotary chair capable of inducing vestibular nystagmus for perspective usage in aviation training
abstract: Spatial orientation is very important during flight for the pilot and his ability to correctly perform several parallel tasks related to piloting, navigation and communication. In the event that the pilot loses his own spatial orientation, he must rely solely on the on-board instruments, increasing his workload and the likelihood that the pilot will make a mistake. Further, flight illusions are associated with the loss of spatial orientation and may cause the pilot to perceive inconsistent information about his or her position. Despite the fact that loss of spatial orientation may be commonly encountered by civilian pilots, they are not prepared for these situations as part of their practical training. Although full-flight simulators adapted to induce illusions can be utilized in this context, they are expensive and essentially unused in the training of civilian pilots. This has led to the proposal of a potentially usable and cost-effective technical solution that could be employed in inducing certain types of illusions. Therefore, the article specifically deals with the design of a rotary chair suitable for inducing vestibular nystagmus and the validation of this solution, along with an introduction to the practicality of this solution in the aviation training and research environment.

articleTitle: UAV Operators’ Cognition and Automation: Comprehensive Measurements
abstract: This research investigates cognitive and physiological dynamics in UAV operators using ECG devices for comprehensive monitoring. By integrating diverse automation levels, operator expertise, and physiological measurements, nuanced interactions between operators and UAV technology emerge. Findings highlight the link between automation complexity and physiological responses, evident in heart rate profiles. ECG devices enable real-time heart rate monitoring, revealing patterns aligned with varying automation levels. Manual control scenarios (Level 0) exhibit heightened heart rate variability, suggesting cognitive demand. Increasing automation leads to reduced heart rate variation, potentially mitigating cognitive load. Outcomes underscore automation’s transformative impact on unmanned aviation, enhancing performance and decision-making. ECG integration bolsters empirical foundations, guiding interface design, training, and operational protocols in the dynamic UAV landscape.

articleTitle: The Ergonomic Design of the Tower Simulator Concept for the Training Needs of Air Traffic Control Students
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to propose an ergonomic concept of the workplace for training students - air traffic controllers at the Faculty of Aeronautics Technical University of Kosice with an emphasis on a complex of ergonomic aspects that affect the efficiency of work, the level of safety, fatigue, and performance. The topic touches on 3D software, programs for modeling and design, through which it is possible to carry out the conceptual design of the simulator workplace. In the process of providing an air traffic control service, the controller as a person is the most important factor for the safety, performance, and quality of the service provided, which mainly depends on his ability, speed, and skills. The tower workplace in real traffic has its local specifics in different phases of the day, geographical orientation, layout, floor plan, and height of the tower. In the case of tower control simulation, we identify the need to design a typified workplace that can also correlate with new trends, where the main task is to create a homogenized remote tower control workplace that would reflect current legislative and ergonomic requirements and would be used in simulated and in real operation. The advantage of this workplace would be its uniformity when applying the design to other simulation centers of tower control.

articleTitle: Alternative Fuels for Small-scale Turbojet Engines: A Review.
abstract: This paper presents a brief review on the alternative aviation fuels and their impact on small-scale turbojet engines. In addition, perspective alternative fuels for each transport sector are presented, highlighting the advantages and disadvantages of these fuels. Individual production pathways certified for alternative aviation fuels are described, while the maximum possible percentage of these fuels is also indicated.

articleTitle: Analyzing ADS-B Systems and Channel Occupancy: Enhancing UAV Control and Aviation Safety through Airspace Management
abstract: This paper examines the impact of transponder occupancy on aviation safety and efficiency. Using data from the European Monitoring of Interrogators and Transponders network and historical records, it investigates Mode S transponder overload and explores challenges posed by drone integration in shared airspace. The paper suggests “detect and avoid” technologies and Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast systems as potential solutions. It emphasizes the need for innovative approaches, including artificial intelligence and flexible airspace allocation, to address congestion and enhance safety in the evolving aviation landscape. Through data analysis and literature review, this research provides insights into transponder occupancy challenges and their implications.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Airport’s Airbridge Operations and Internal Setting
abstract: In this paper we investigate opportunities to enhance the existing operational procedures of airbridge operators. Prior to exploring potential improvements, a simulation model of the Prague Airport north apron infrastructure is developed using AnyLogic simulation software. The primary focus of optimization revolves around human resource allocation. The optimization of airbridge operator processes is achieved through various configurations of the developed simulation model. Comparative analysis with the current operational framework is conducted, followed by a thorough evaluation of the results. Furthermore, recommendations are provided on how to implement such processes in practice to ensure that airbridge operators and necessary equipment are always available in sufficient quantities, thereby achieving the desired quality of aircraft handling. Versatility of the model also allows for future improvement and its application to optimize the configuration of aircraft ground handling processes.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of the Change in the Radiation Characteristics of the Communication and Telemetry Antenna of the UAV Used as a Supplementary Rescue Device for SAR and HEMS
abstract: Using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as supplementary devices for saving human lives extended significantly in a few years. Specifically designed and homologated UAVs are mainly used, but an affordable alternative is also available in conventional UAVs that have undergone appropriate modification. However, the modifications carried out on unmanned vehicles can disrupt the communication and telemetry channel, which is necessary for the mission’s correct command and control by the pilot-operator from the ground. For this reason, every mechanical modification and improvement needs to be tested before a real flight test - ideally in a simulation environment. The presented paper is devoted to modifying the chosen UAV, then simulation and analysing the change in the antenna’s radiation characteristics of the UAV communication-control (telemetry) module, adjusted to the form of the supplementary rescue device, which should be used mainly as the Helicopter Emergency Medical Service (HEMS) support.

articleTitle: Design Concept of Low-Cost Magnetometric System for Small UAVs and CubeSats
abstract: The paper presents the design concept of low-cost magnetometric system that has been developed at the Faculty of Aeronautics at the Technical University of Kosice. The design is based on the achieved results in the ongoing development of both the relax-type magnetometers and time difference microwire magnetometers. Both of the mentioned types use the conversion of magnetic field measurement into the measurement of time intervals difference. The cores of the sensors are made from amorphous magnetic ribbons or magnetic microwire, the proposed design is intended to be operating primarily with bistable magnetic microwires. The design presented in the paper follows the ongoing research and introduces possible functionality back-ups.

articleTitle: Airline Occurrence Report Form Based on System-Theoretic Process Analysis
abstract: The aim of this paper is to propose a structured approach to define the occurrence reporting form in an international airline. For this purpose, the System-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA) was used. The method serves for analyzing the flight operations of the air carrier and subsequently for the prediction of causal factors relevant for the operations. The result is a sample reporting form for events during taxiing and take-off, which are subject to mandatory reporting under the European legislation. The form was tested by commercial aircraft pilots. The obtained data were analyzed, evaluated and placed in the context of operating conditions. Based on the results obtained, it can be said that the proposed reporting forms provide safety department staff with enhanced insight into reported occurrences and can be used to apply targeted safety measures.

articleTitle: A STAMP-based Risk Register for Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul Organisations
abstract: Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) organizations are one of the pillars of aviation safety. They ensure the airworthiness of aircraft in accordance with regulatory requirements. In Europe, until the recent changes in legislation, safety was part of quality and compliance management. Today, MROs are required to implement a Safety Management System (SMS). The paper focuses on MRO hazard and risk register, proposing a sample register with a procedure how to develop it. The proposed solution integrates with other parts of the integrated management system, such as quality control or occupational health and safety. The hazard and risk register was proposed using the recent approach of the System-Theoretic Accident Model and Processes (STAMP) accident causality model, suitable for complex sociotechnical systems, which are typical in the aviation today. The proposed solution allows the assessment of the system as a whole, which leads to the identification of new types of hazards and structuring of the existing ones. The presented study was performed with two European MROs to evaluate and validate its outputs.

articleTitle: Assessment and evaluation of suitable aircraft for specific approved training organization
abstract: The main aim of the paper is to introduce a particular approved training organization as well as initial criteria. The paper is focused on detailed characterization and technical specification of chosen aircraft that meet criteria, their usability, safety, and economy. The contribution of the paper is to use Saaty’s method as a tool for objective assessment and evaluation of selected aircraft suitable for training purposes in a particular training organization and subsequently applying the procedure to the one of the airplanes.

articleTitle: Environmental impacts of aviation and opportunities for “green” energy solutions
abstract: The aim of the publication is to analyse the dominant energy consumption characteristics, properties and energy trends present in aviation and airports by presenting the main energy sources and consumers. It presents possible solutions for energy saving, related energy efficiency measures, and environmental options that are currently available or planned in the future using renewable and alternative energy sources in order to reduce harmful environmental impacts.

articleTitle: Mobile Monitoring System for the Protection of the Area of Interest
abstract: The article describes the design and solution of a mobile monitoring system for the collection of data from freestanding sensory elements freely distributed in the area of interest into a complex sensory network in connection with an online system for the collection and evaluation of the obtained data, initially with the aim of protecting an isolated group of the population from the spread of viral diseases or vice versa protecting people from an isolated group identified as a source of risk. The authors present the architecture of the proposed system, its properties and application use. Thanks to its universality, the proposed and further developed system is generally applicable for application use in various areas of interest or further research. The proposed solution of the monitoring system for securing areas of interest is original especially from the point of view of its mobility, universality and independence from the use of sensors.

articleTitle: The method of detecting dangerous attacks in the network operation of the flight training department against cyber threats
abstract: The aim of the article is to present the results from the analysis of network traffic obtained with the help of the GREYCORTEX MENDEL tool at the Department of Flight Training of the Faculty of Aeronautics TUKE, which serves for advanced analysis of network traffic and detection of hidden malware and anomalies using machine learning and artificial intelligence. The research presents the results of software analysis - GREYCORTEX Mendel for attack detection and prevention of security incidents that could disrupt the stability of the information network of the Department of Flight Training. The article presents a tool to visualize the network traffic of all connected devices of the institution, whose communication is then analyzed and filtered as needed to ensure reliable connection and security. The test operation of this tool was carried out at the Faculty of Aeronautics - Technical University of Kosice (LF TUKE) at the Department of Flight Training. The results of the analysis of network traffic with the help of GREYCORTEX Mendel helped us to discover how the selected network can be attacked. Dangerous threats could be identified and filtered out of network traffic to secure network infrastructure and protect sensitive data.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Risks of UAV Flights that Deter Wild Animals in Airport Areas
abstract: The research was conducted on the actual task of assessing the risks of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) flights to achieve the goals of scaring off wild animals and performing a safe UAV flight in the vicinity of the airport during the task. As a result, a normalized assessment of the risks of UAV flights and a linguistic level of flight safety in the deterrence of wild animals is obtained, which will allow making proactive decisions regarding the controllability of UAV flight processes in the deterrence of wild animals at airports. In the study, for the first time, an information expert model was developed for the assessment of the risks of UAV flights that deter wild animals in the vicinity of airports. For the first time, a fuzzy UAV flight risk assessment model is developed using inputs from an information model, using intelligent knowledge analysis, fuzzy set theory, and one-dimensional membership functions. An example of assessment is illustrated. The conducted research will be a useful tool to support the adoption of the implementation of UAV flight safety within the biological protection of airports.

articleTitle: Enhancing Unmanned Aerial Systems Data Communication through Mobile Networks
abstract: A key factor for effectively operating unmanned aerial systems is ensuring reliable and fast communication between the ground station and the unmanned aircraft vehicle. The choice of communication channel results from specific requirements for data rate and range of the vehicle. Currently, the use of cellular mobile networks is marginal in commercial unmanned systems, although these networks have excellent coverage and harbor enormous potential for communication flows within systems. This study presents the concept of a real-time two-way data link communication between an unmanned aircraft vehicle and a ground station with the implementation of the Micro Air Vehicle Link (MAVLink) open communication protocol, using an experimental setup that includes a Raspberry Pi, a Long-Term Evolution (LTE) module, and Pixhawk flight controller. According to the established methodology, the connection speed and robustness of the whole concept were verified. The study’s results demonstrated that using mobile networks can significantly improve the communication between the subsystems of the unmanned aerial system as a whole and provide a solution for more reliable and efficient unmanned flying. This research contributes to the advancement of unmanned aircraft subsystems and their capacity for real-time long-range communication with ground stations, thus enhancing these vehicles’ operational efficiency and safety.

articleTitle: New Personality Evaluation of Pilot Candidates in Czech Air Force
abstract: Pilot selection has been a topic since the beginning of aviation, both in civil and military aviation. The first research was carried out before the First World War and has gained importance, especially in the last 20 years, due to the dynamic growth of civil air transport. The selection of military pilots in the Czech Air Force environment takes place within the framework of the admission procedure for study at the University of Defence (UoD) in the specialization of military pilot (MP). The selection includes medical tests, psychological tests, and knowledge tests. This paper aims to verify the suitability of using the NEO Five-Factor Inventory (NEO-FFI) test battery in a shortened form to design and implement a new objective system for selecting candidates for the military pilot specialization. Current MP specialization students (n=51) and candidates in the 2022/2023 academic year (n=35) were tested. The results showed that most students tested (82%) scored low on the Neuroticism scale, and 16% are in the broader average range. On the Conscientiousness scale, a majority of the students (63%) scored high, 37% of the students were in the normal range, and none of the respondents were in the below-average range. The analysis shows that 55% of the subjects have low Neuroticism scores and high Conscientiousness scores. The pilot testing has fulfilled its purpose; there has been a validation of the tools that can be used to define the prerequisites to achieve the desired abilities and skills for the MP specialization. This form may be used to select suitable candidates for the MP specialization in the future.

articleTitle: Safety Assessment of Cessna 172 Flight Procedures With System-Theoretic Process Analysis
abstract: Flight procedures are one of the main pillars for the safe performance of a flight. However, sometimes flight procedures must be modified. The need to modify them may arise from operational experience or a safety study. One of the methods that can be used to perform a safety study for the purpose is System-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA). The goal of this paper was to perform a safety assessment of the Cessna 172 flight procedures based on a proactive systems approach to safety, using STPA. The goal was to identify potential safety issues related to selected flight procedures and to propose corrective measures or safety recommendations that could be used in practice. The results show how to work with STPA in the context of flight procedures and what measures or recommendations emerged from the analysis for the Cessna 172 flight procedures. The analysis confirmed the possibility of using system safety approach in general aviation to assess flight procedures and usefulness of its results.

articleTitle: Predictability of In-block Time Deviations: An Analysis of Operational Data, Tactical Flight Models and Meteorological Information
abstract: Efficient airport operations are vital for ensuring the seamless flow of aircraft and passengers. However, real-world airport operations often deviate from meticulously crafted plans, necessitating dynamic resource allocation. These challenges become particularly pronounced during peak operational periods when butter capacity is limited. To address these issues, we conducted an analysis utilizing operational data from the airport, along with Filed Tactical Flight Model and Current Tactical Flight Model data, as well as meteorological information. Our study primarily focuses on incoming flights at Prague Airport, where we employed regression analysis, forward parameter selection, and a brute-force approach to identify key parameters. These parameters significantly enhance the predictability of in-block time deviations and delay caused in individual phases of the flight. Our model successfully explains up to 96 % of the variability in the data. In summary, this research aims to optimize airport operations by bridging the gap between planned and actual in-block times, ultimately enhancing airport efficiency. The comprehensive analysis of various data elements offers valuable insights for airport management and decision-makers.

articleTitle: Analysis of the introduction of Prague-Kbely Airport as an alternative airport for low-cost companies to Václav Havel Airport
abstract: Nowadays, it is an undeniable fact that the cost of operating airplanes is increasing. Airlines are therefore looking for ways to save with the least possible impact on their operations and passengers. One option used primarily by low-cost airlines is the use of smaller local airports with lower fees compared to large international airports. Václav Havel Airport is considered a large international airport in Prague, and the nearest possible alternative airports for low-cost airlines are at least 100 km away. This article analyzes the possibility of introducing civil air transport to the Kbely military airport and thereby creating an alternative airport to Václav Havel Airport directly in Prague. A comparison of capacities, airport facilities with a focus on runway options and handling of Airbus A320Neo and Boeing 737 NG aircraft was carried out, and at the same time, airport fees for these types of aircraft were compared. The result of the analysis is that Prague-Kbely Airport has the capacity and possibilities to receive and handle aircraft of the specified types, and in the event that low-cost companies divert part of the traffic from Václav Havel Airport to Kbely Airport, the annual savings would amount to more than 50 % with minimal impact on passenger comfort.

articleTitle: Options for the recovery of human resource management in the aviation industry
abstract: The air transport system is a source of great economic activity and creates a number of jobs that are directly related to the air transport process, air carriers, airports, air navigation service providers, and ground handling providers. In this article, we focus on the area of human resource management recovery in European international airports with a closer focus on aircraft ground handling divisions. A detailed study was conducted on past available studies to understand COVID-19 and its relationship with employment trends. An analysis of the statistical data of the companies involved in the research activity was carried out. The objective of the empirical, quantitative research is to point out the possibility of a strategy for the recovery of human resources from the consequences of COVID-19 on the European air transport market, implemented by the method of scientific observation.
